results.hypothesis_statement: In the synthetic parametric strategy, increasing signal_threshold decreases trade frequency because fewer signal observations satisfy the strategy's eligibility condition, holding all other parameters and the synthetic input path fixed.

Within a point-in-time, survivorship-bias-free universe of listed common equities, stocks with higher trailing 20-trading-day adjusted-close returns will have higher subsequent 5-trading-day adjusted-close returns in cross-sectional tests.

For MES futures, a higher best-level bid-ask order-book imbalance measured at the end of a 1-second interval predicts a more positive mid-price return over the subsequent 1-second interval, while a lower imbalance predicts a more negative subsequent return.

In a synthetic parametric strategy with all non-threshold parameters held fixed, increasing the absolute signal-entry threshold will monotonically decrease the number of executed entry trades, and variation in that threshold will explain more trade-count variation than variation in any individually tested non-threshold parameter over the specified parameter ranges.

For the CME E-mini S&P 500 (ES) front-month futures contract, sessions whose first 30 minutes have volume above the trailing 60-session 80th percentile for that same time-of-day are more likely to have a close-to-first-30-minute return in the same direction as the first-30-minute return than sessions with first-30-minute volume at or below that threshold.

For US-listed liquid common equities during regular continuous trading, a positive top-of-book depth imbalance—bid size minus ask size normalized by total displayed size—predicts a positive 1-second future midquote return after conditioning on quoted spread and recent trade-sign imbalance.

For synthetic AR(1)-GARCH(1,1) return processes with a fixed innovation distribution and fixed unconditional variance, increasing GARCH volatility persistence will increase the out-of-sample calibration error of an AR(1)-only one-step predictive distribution, even when the AR coefficient is held constant.
